A real back edge can only be found while its entry is still on the `open` stack. A pending entry that is no longer on the stack belongs to a concurrent branch, not an ancestor.

**Fix**: `Entry` gains a `done` promise, set when the entry's parse returns a promise. A hit on an entry that has `done` set and is not on `open` now waits for it, then replays its recorded issues into the current payload. The existing back-edge path is unchanged for entries still on `open`. Nothing changes for synchronous parses.

**Tests**: I added a regression case to `classic/tests/recursive-types.test.ts`. It checks that the union rejects the bad input and still accepts a valid nested input. The existing recursive and lazy tests also pass.

**Limit**: a real cycle that closes only after an async hop would now wait on itself and hang. I did not test that case. It needs cyclic input data plus an async boundary on the cycle path, and the alternative of reparsing instead would recurse without end on the same input.

**Not measured**: the three-axes check in the repo instructions (runtime, memory, bundle size). The change adds one optional field per entry and one `open.includes` call, only on a pending hit.

**Confidence**: High on the cause and on the reproduction. Medium on the async-hop cycle edge case above.
